text:
alexa: Heads-up: saw requests with x-model-alias: 'gpt-open-v1' routing to 'gpt-open-v2' when route has pin=true. Repro on prod around 10:02 UTC.

mike: @alexa can you paste the raw headers? which gateway version?

alexa: here's the request headers i captured: `Accept: application/json, x-model-alias: gpt-open-v1, x-tenant-id: acme, x-routing-mode: prefer-cost` — gateway reported selected_model=gpt-open-v2 in the trace.

jun: That sounds like the header precedence change we shipped in canary but didn't roll back. We intentionally moved route.pin above per-request override for safety during rollouts.

sara: We also hit a compatibility dimension: pinned variants sometimes have different KV-cache/key layout. If a request-level override picks a model incompatible with the cached state, you'll break decoders. Do we check compatibility before honoring overrides?

mike: Current selection logic (roughly):

```python
# pseudo-selection
if route.pin:
    selected = route.pin
elif headers.get('x-model-version'):
    selected = headers['x-model-version']
elif headers.get('x-model-alias'):
    selected = resolve_alias(headers['x-model-alias'])
else:
    selected = route.default_alias
```

That ordering makes route.pin > headers. Seems like the change in canary reversed our previous expectation that request headers should be able to override for short-lived debugging.

jun: I think correct behavior is: headers (explicit version) should win, then route.pin, then alias fallback — but with two constraints: 1) only allow request-level override if a compatibility check passes, 2) only for requests with override_ttl <= 5m or tenant in allowlist.

alexa: Suggested policy: accept x-model-version or x-model-alias override only when: `route.enable_request_override = true` AND `headers['x-override-ttl'] <= 300` AND `compatibility_check(selected, route.pin) == True`. Also require audit log entry for every override (tenant, user, reason).

sara: Add telemetry counters: `header_override_attempts`, `header_override_denied`, `header_override_applied`, and a hist for `override_latency_penalty`. Console should show a per-route metric for % of requests with request-level overrides and list last 10 override audit events.

mike: I'll send a tiny patch: change precedence to check explicit headers first, then route.pin, but gate header application with compat check. Add unit tests for alias->pin mismatch and an integration test that asserts x-redwood-routing-reason header is set to either `pin` | `header_override` | `fallback`. Also introduce feature flag `route.enable_request_override` default=false.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: service/gateway v4.3.2 -> canary at 1794043400, prod rollout scheduled in 30m if canary passes.

alexa: Good. Also can we make the Console UX show the active model at the top of the route page (pinned vs default) and allow an operator to temporarily accept request-overrides for a route via a toggle with a TTL? Need about 1-click enable + audit message.

jun: Note-to-self: ensure compatibility matrix lives in model metadata (kv_cache_schema_version, quantization flags). selection logic should call `model_compatibility(route.pin, candidate)` before applying override. If incompatible, record `header_override_denied` and return routing reason `pin_incompatible`.

mike: I'll open the PR and link tests. Follow-ups: docs update for precedence, add e2e in infra-tests, and add dashboard tiles.

alexa: Thanks — i put the failing trace in #incidents just in case. :thumbsup:

sara: Adding a quick dashboard card request to product analytics for override counts per-tenant.

jun: final implementation note: add response header `x-redwood-routing-reason: header_override|pin|default|pin_incompatible` so downstream clients can debug.

mike: owning the ticket, will ping when canary is up.
